text: Hello students, welcome back.Please get your student's book and your worksheet ready.In today's lesson, we are going to talk about a grammatical item and then practice some writing.Do you still remember the dialogue between the kangaroo and the crew?This is my student Eric's work.I like the dialogue he created.In the dialogue, the characters take turns to speak and move their ideas along.Eric's words make the characters' personalities and emotions alive to listeners.Do you notice the punctuation marks used at the end of these sentences?They are exclamation marks, 感叹号, so we call these sentences exclamations, 感叹句.An exclamation is a word or phrase that you say to show a strong feeling or emotion, such as happiness, surprise, pity or gratitude, etc.It usually ends with an exclamation mark.So, what feelings or emotions can you read from the exclamations in the dialogue?Look at the four sentences said by the kangaroo.I think the sentence I heard what Gorg said implies that the kangaroo was a bit worried about the crew's situation.The kangaroo must be surprised at what Gorg said to the crew and felt sorry about them.And the other three sentences show that the kangaroo was quite excited about the plan, and we can feel his confidence in his plan.You understand the dialogue well.What about the two sentences said by Captain King?The sentence, yes, he's going to kill us, shows that the captain was angry and maybe a bit worried too.But later, after hearing the kangaroo's plan, he got excited.We can read his excitement from the sentences.Well done.So, how did Peter feel after hearing the plan?He was happy about the plan, right?He used the word wow in a sentence beginning with what to show his joy.Exclamations are not always complete sentences.We can sometimes use one word exclamation.For example, ouch is the sound you make when you feel sudden pain.When you taste something good, you will say yummy.In this case, they are called interjections.But today we will mainly focus on the exclamations beginning with what and how.An example is what Peter said at the end of the dialogue.This sentence begins with what followed by a noun phrase, a great idea, and ends with an exclamation mark.A what exclamation usually goes into this order.What plus article an plus adjective plus noun plus subject plus verb plus exclamation mark.Let's take a look at the examples.What a great idea it is.However, if there is more than one great idea, leave out the article a and put s at the end of idea.Then change its is into they are.When people exclaim what good luck we have, a can't be used here because luck is an uncountable noun.And this part is the noun phrase.The noun can be a singular noun, a plural noun, or an uncountable noun.Very often, we cut the subject and the verb to make the exclamation short.What a great idea.What great ideas.What good luck.The speaker and the listeners already know what great idea or ideas they are talking about, or they know who have the good luck.Sometimes we even don't have an adjective to modify the noun, such as what fun or what fun it will be.A how exclamation goes into this order.How plus adjective or adverb plus subject plus verb plus exclamation mark.How helpful the kangaroos are.Captain King's crew already know he is talking about the kangaroos.He can just say how helpful.When Gork was asleep, his snoring noise shook the cave.At that time, Captain King felt shocked and said, how loudly Gork snored.Now, practice time.Here I've got some jumbled sentences.The words in the sentences are jumbled up.Your task is to form the correct sentences.You must use each word.Ready?How is it going?Can you read the sentences for us?Read it with emotions, okay?What's a perfect plan Captain King had?How quickly the crew left the cave?What strange friends you have got?How powerful the laser torch is?You got them correct.And good pronunciation and intonation.Thank you.Sometimes, when we are doing multiple choice questions, we find it hard to tell whether to put what or how in the blank.Look at this item.Which will you choose?An easy way to do this is to find the subject and the verb first, which is it is in this sentence.Put a line before the subject.If there is a noun before the subject,then the exclamation begins with what.If there is an adjective or adverb before the subject,then we put how at the beginning.In this sentence, the word before the subject, it,is interesting, an adjective.So the answer should be how.Look at these sentences.What can be filled in the blanks in the blue parts?First, find the subject and the verb.Then, judge the part of speech.Tidy, well, noisy are adjectives and adverbs.We should put how in the left blank.Fun, beautiful flowers and a lovely panda are noun or noun phrases.What can be put in the right blank?Sometimes the subject and the verb are omitted.Then the last word can be the clue.Like how noisy.What a lovely panda.Noisy is an adjective, while panda is a noun.Let's do more practice.Task 2 on your worksheet.Filling in the blanks with what or how.Add a or n if necessary.Remember to find the subject first, then put a line before it.Please go.Let's check the answers.Have you got them correct?Look at sentence 4.Writing is an uncountable noun.So no a or n is needed.And the last sentence, the word has is in plural form.No a or n is needed.Rita, can you read sentences 2 and 5 for us?How fast the UFO was flying.What big heads the aliens have.What emotion do you think the sentences express?To express surprise, I think.The speaker has seen neither creatures with such big heads, nor such a fast UFO.I think so too.Exclamations are often used when people feel surprised at something.Look at this picture.A woman was standing behind a tree.How did she look?She seemed very surprised.Have a guess.What was she surprised at?And what would she say?Maybe she saw a car accident.Cars got crashed, some people were injured, and the traffic was blocked.She would say, what's a terrible accident?Maybe she saw a large field of red roses.And she would say, how beautiful the roses are.Good guess.Now let's see what she was really surprised at.Rita, please.She saw Gork, the huge one-eyed alien.But did she know that its name was Gork?I don't think so.What could she call it?She could just call it a monster or an alien.And she would say, what's a huge monster?Good choice.What did she see the monster doing?She saw it approaching a house.Was it Captain King's house?At the end of the reading part, we knew that Captain King escaped from Gorkand went back to the earth.Just as he was telling his story to his friends,a huge figure was moving silently towards his house.Right.The huge figure was Gork.He wanted to take his revenge.And the woman saw what happened.Actually, she was Mabel Wong, a reporter and a neighbor of Captain King.When she was passing the captain's garden last night,she saw the strange figure and watched what happened next.I will show you some pictures.Read and try to summarize what happened.Eric, what do you think the story is about?The alien tried to hurt Captain King,but the captain ran away and drove his car into a tunnel.The alien followed, but it was too big to enter the tunnel.Soon the soldiers arrived, and the alien had to leave.Luckily, Captain King escaped successfully.Thank you, Eric.You gave us a good summary.Since Mabel was a reporter and an eyewitness of the incident,she decided to write a report about it,and she needed to give a detailed reportto help readers form a vivid picture in their minds,even if they were not on the scene or unable to see these pictures.So, how can we describe the event in detail?One effective way is to describe your senses,that is, what you see, hear, smell, taste or feel in the event.They are sensory details.Let's have a try.Suppose you are Mabel Wang.What could you see in the second picture?I could see the alien kicking the walls, trying to break them down.Captain King and his friends were running out of the house.What could you hear at that time?I could hear a loud bang.And how did you feel?I was scared and frightened by the sound.Good.Look at the third picture.What did you see?Captain King was running towards a car.He wanted to jump into it and drive off.Then what did the alien do?The alien followed him in his spaceship.Did the spaceship catch up with Captain King's car?Almost.But then Captain King raced into a tunnel and took cover there.Good words.Racing into means move very fast.Chōng rù.And take cover means find protection from attack.Duò bì.But how did you know?The tunnel seemed a long distance away from where you lived.I was really curious about what would happen to the captain, so I followed them.Great.Sometimes the sensory details can help you connect the pictures.Why do you think Captain King drove into the tunnel, Rita?I think it's because the tunnel was too small for the spaceship to enter.The alien landed the spaceship nearby and got out, but he was still too big to enter the tunnel.How did you feel at that time?I thought it was really clever of Captain King to enter the tunnel.At the same time, I was also eager to know what the alien was going to do.Did you see what happened then?Luckily, some soldiers arrived.I thought the captain must have caught them, and the alien seemed very frightened.What did the alien do then?The alien ran back to its spaceship and flew away.Did you think the alien would just give up his revenge?I don't think so, because as I left, the alien shouted to Captain King,I'll be back for you.And Captain King replied, I'll be waiting for you, Gork.I'm afraid Captain King should get prepared for another attack.Yes, it doesn't seem to be the end.And I guess that's why Mabel Wong wrote the report, to create suspense, right?Before we start writing the report, let's think about what an eyewitness report is like.Different from a news report or a police report, it is a first-person description of an event that you personally witnessed.Its text type is a narrative writing.Its purpose is to provide specific details about the event in a clear and brief way.From the definition, in what point of view is an eyewitness report written?Yes, we use the first person to write the report.And what tense should the witness use to talk about an event?The simple past tense.And the audience is average readers like you and me.When you write an eyewitness report, you need to understand your audience.It will decide your type of writing, the goal you want to achieve, and what point of view and tense you will use.You should study the pictures carefully, and use sensory details to describe the pictures vividly.And don't forget to consider the connection between pictures.Now let's look at the writing task.It's task 3 on your worksheet.Complete Mabel's report by using the details you collect from the pictures.If necessary, use some exclamations.You can also find a checklist on your worksheet.It can help you check and make necessary changes.Let's get started.Time is up.Erik, could you please share your work with us?Yesterday evening, when I was walking past the garden of my neighbour, the famous basement captain King,I saw an alien in his garden.It was a huge one-eyed monster.It approached his house and kicked the walls hard, trying to break them down.The loud bang really scared me.Then I found Captain King running out immediately, jumping into his car and driving off.I saw an alien in his garden.I found Captain King running out immediately, jumping into his car and driving off.I was really curious and also worried about the captain, so I followed them.Before I could catch up, he raced into a tunnel and took cover there.It was obviously too small for the spaceship to enter.The alien had to land nearby, get out and walk to the tunnel, but it was still too big.What a clever trick.At that moment, some soldiers arrived.The alien was frightened.It got into its spaceship and flew away.As it left, the alien shouted to Captain King, I'll be back for you.C
